column3: Lunpa's closed. You still\nwant to enter?{end_now}
Then turn around.\nNo one gets in.{end_wait}
You came all this way?\nThat's unfortunate.\nTurn back.{end_wait}
You're not from Kalay,\nare you?{end_now}
The last group said that.\nDidn't make them honest.\nLeave before I call help.{end_wait}
Here for Hammet,\naren't you?{end_now}
We'll release him soon.\nThat's what Dodonpa\nordered us to say.{end_wait}
Don't lie to me.\nNo one comes this far\nwithout a reason.{end_wait}

They might try the cave
west of Lunpa.
They won't get through.{page_break}The gate's too heavy
to lift from outside.{end_wait}
Even if they reach\nthe cave, it's useless.\nThat gate opens inside.{end_wait}
Have you been here\nbefore?{end_now}
I don't know your face.\nNo one here does.{end_wait}
New to Dodonpa's gang?\nBetter learn the rules\nbefore you get hurt.{end_wait}

The caravan was taken,
and now we're prisoners
in our own village.{page_break}No one can leave.
No one comes in.
Even the roads are closed.{end_wait}
Did Dodonpa really\ntake Hammet for ransom?{end_now}
Then the rumors are true.\nHow could they do that?{end_wait}
I wanted to believe\nit was only a rumor.\nPerhaps I was wrong.{end_wait}
Donpa's too old to lead.\nHis men follow Dodonpa\ninstead.{end_wait}
Lunpa and Donpa were\nmen this town respected.\nPeople forget that now.{end_wait}

Donpa doesn't know
what his son's been doing.{page_break}If he knew,
maybe he'd put an end
to all of this.{end_wait}
You want to see Donpa?{end_now}
He's in the fortress.\nYou'd have to pass\nDodonpa's guards.{end_wait}
Then don't go near it.\nPeople who enter\ndon't always return.{end_wait}

The inn's chef takes
meals to the fortress.{page_break}Even he comes back
shaking. They watch
everyone inside.{end_wait}
Stay back. That's an order.{end_wait}
I served Donpa for years.\nHow did his son become\nthe man he is?{end_wait}
Nothing gets past me.\nNot even a mouse.{end_wait}
The gates are sealed.\nEven an honest trader\nwould be turned away.{end_wait}
Hammet came here himself.\nWhat could he have\nbeen thinking?{end_wait}

They took the ransom.
So why hasn't Hammet
been released?{page_break}Kalay keeps paying.
Someone's growing rich.{end_wait}

Lunpa died when Donpa
was still young.
He never got over it.{page_break}He spoiled Dodonpa
to spare him that pain.
Look where it led.{end_wait}

Dodonpa takes what
he wants from everyone.{page_break}If the town gets nothing,
why should his men
have everything?{end_wait}

Dodonpa keeps his father
away from the streets.{page_break}Donpa can't stop
what he doesn't know
is happening here.{end_wait}
Guards day and night.\nThey've made the fortress\na prison for us all.{end_wait}
That poor chef comes back\npale every time.\nI'd never go inside.{end_wait}

Keep Hammet locked up.
Kalay will keep paying.
Dodonpa thought of that.{page_break}He really is clever.
I'll have money
for the rest of my life.{end_wait}
Only a shadow\ncould get past me.{end_wait}

My grandfather traveled
with Lunpa himself.{page_break}He'd hate to see
the town he helped build
turned into this.{end_wait}
We live in Lunpa.\nThat doesn't mean\nwe serve Dodonpa.{end_wait}
There was a time\nwe could leave our homes\nwithout fear.{end_wait}
They want us to join\nDodonpa's men.\nI won't do it.{end_wait}

Donpa built the fortress.
He knew how to keep
intruders out.{page_break}Now those walls
are keeping us in.{end_wait}
Only the inn's chef\nis allowed inside.\nHe brings the meals.{end_wait}
Every corner is watched.\nHard to move anywhere\nwithout being seen.{end_wait}

The chef started
making deliveries
after the caravan came.{page_break}Someone inside
has to be eating
those meals.{end_wait}

Lunpa traveled south
when the great flood came.
He never returned.{page_break}The waters took him.
At least that's
what we've been told.{end_wait}
Lunpa was traveling\nwith a man called Babi\nwhen the flood struck.{end_wait}
They say the flood\nswallowed whole towns.\nNo one knows how many.{end_wait}
Babi? What sort\nof name is that?{end_wait}

No road, no customers.
This shop can't last.{page_break}Dodonpa eats well.
The rest of us
can go hungry.{end_wait}
I've still got armor.\nWhen Lunpa opens again,\ncome see me.{end_wait}

I've stocked up,
but nothing can reach us.{page_break}Even the traders
are suffering now.
Their goods can't move.{end_wait}
Want to stay at my inn?{end_now}
You must be joking.\nGo sleep at home!{end_wait}
I know.\nNo one wants a room\nin a sealed town.{end_wait}

Hammet's ransom
made Dodonpa wealthy.{page_break}We haven't seen
a coin of it.
Just empty rooms.{end_wait}
We keep the rooms clean.\nNo one comes to stay.\nStill, we keep working.{end_wait}
Want to hear about\nmy trip to the fortress?{end_now}

They blindfolded me.
I walked a long way
through cold air.{page_break}My steps echoed.
We were underground.
I know that much.{end_wait}

I was relieved
to see daylight again.{page_break}They called the prisoner
Hammet. I never saw
his face clearly.{end_wait}
I won't close this inn.\nNot while the people\nof Lunpa still need it.{end_wait}
He took a man for ransom.\nHe'd sell the whole town\nif someone offered enough.{end_wait}
Empty rooms, empty tables.\nI wonder how long\nthey'll keep paying me.{end_wait}
I heard the prisoner's\nvoice when I served him.\nHe sounded so tired.{end_wait}

Dodonpa's done
terrible things.{page_break}But the people of Lunpa
aren't all his servants.
They still need us.{end_wait}
We can't abandon Lunpa.\nDodonpa's men are\nwatching the roads.{end_wait}
Another week like this\nand I'll have to\nclose my shop.{end_wait}
I should have bought\nmore armor when\nthe roads were open.{end_wait}
All this stock,\nand already I'm running\nlow.{page_break}I can't order more.{end_wait}
No one enters Lunpa\nwithout Dodonpa's order.\nGo back.{end_wait}
If anyone slips inside,\nDodonpa will punish\nthe guards first.{end_wait}
